doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Bob Thiele staying out of the way
summary: Thiele was an unobtrusive producer, and told a story of Duke Ellington declining a second take with Coltrane.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: You know it takes an open-minded producer I think to just, or at least someone who just stays out of the way.

Monk that’s the whole key. ‘Cause Bob Thiele never got in the way but I guess you know he — Bob Thiele produced all those records by John Coltrane. And then he told me a story about the record he produced with John Coltrane and Duke Ellington. And Bob Thiele, you know, if you let him he’d have you doing two and three takes. So Duke Ellington and Trane, they performed the song so Bob came out and said, “Okay let’s do another take.” Duke Ellington told him, said, “No, it’s going to be different anyway.”
